summary: Obfuscated preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime to execute large opaque payload in an ESLint config package
details: The package ships an obfuscated preinstall script setup.mjs (javascript-obfuscator hex-identifier renaming and string-array indirection) that, on npm install, downloads the Bun v1.3.13 runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses that alternate runtime to execute a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated payload (rotating string-array indirection, random-token identifier renaming, custom-alphabet decoder) marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`, whose contents are opaque to static analysis. Executing the payload through a freshly downloaded non-Node runtime evades Node-based module resolution and scanning. The declared purpose of the package is an ESLint TypeScript/React configuration, which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time or run an opaque native-runtime payload. The combination of preinstall lifecycle execution, obfuscated dropper, alternate-runtime execution, and a shipped opaque 727 KB executable payload matches the alternate-runtime-dropper attack shape and results in arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
